environment.description: Application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer. The ALB has three listener rules evaluated in priority order: (1) Priority 5: forward /health to target group unconditionally, (2) Priority 10: AWS WAFv2 WebACL association with rule group containing AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (with SizeRestrictions_QUERYSTRING action override to COUNT) and AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet in BLOCK mode, (3) Priority 20: a custom WAFv2 rule using a RegexPatternSet that matches request query strings against pattern `(?i)(?:union\s+select|;\s*(?:drop|alter|insert|update|delete)|'\s*or\s+'|information_schema)` with BLOCK action. The WebACL default action is ALLOW. Additionally, the ECS task role has no S3 or external network permissions, and the VPC has no NAT gateway — the Fargate task runs in a private subnet with no internet egress route, preventing data exfiltration even if a blind injection were somehow crafted to bypass the WAF rules.

config.load_balancer: ALB with HTTPS listener, WAFv2 WebACL attached
config.network: Private subnet, no NAT gateway, no internet gateway route, VPC endpoints for ECR/CloudWatch only
config.compute: ECS Fargate, task role with ecr:GetAuthorizationToken and logs:PutLogEvents only
config.egress: Security group egress limited to VPC endpoints (443 to pl-xxxxxxxx prefix list)
